    74  We define the class `AdmissibleAbsValues K` for a field `K`, which captures the notion of a
    75  family of absolute values on `K` satisfying a product formula.
    76  -/
    77  
    78  /-- A type class capturing an admissible family of absolute values. -/
    79  class AdmissibleAbsValues (K : Type*) [Field K] where
    80    /-- The archimedean absolute values as a multiset of `ℝ`-valued absolute values on `K`. -/
    81    archAbsVal : Multiset (AbsoluteValue K ℝ)
    82    /-- The nonarchimedean absolute values as a set of `ℝ`-valued absolute values on `K`. -/
    83    nonarchAbsVal : Set (AbsoluteValue K ℝ)
    84    /-- The nonarchimedean absolute values are indeed nonarchimedean. -/
    85    isNonarchimedean : ∀ v ∈ nonarchAbsVal, IsNonarchimedean v
    86    /-- Only finitely many (nonarchimedean) absolute values are `≠ 1` for any nonzero `x : K`. -/
    87    hasFiniteMulSupport {x : K} (_ : x ≠ 0) : (fun v : nonarchAbsVal ↦ v.val x).HasFiniteMulSupport
    88    /-- The product formula. The archimedean absolute values are taken with their multiplicity. -/
    89    product_formula {x : K} (_ : x ≠ 0) :
    90        (archAbsVal.map (· x)).prod * ∏ᶠ v : nonarchAbsVal, v.val x = 1
    91  
    92  open AdmissibleAbsValues Real Function
    93  
    94  @[deprecated (since := "2026-03-03")] alias
    95    AdmissibleAbsValues.mulSupport_finite := AdmissibleAbsValues.hasFiniteMulSupport
    96  
    97  attribute [fun_prop] hasFiniteMulSupport
    98  
    99  variable (K : Type*) [Field K] [AdmissibleAbsValues K]
"}]
